nodes.content: Design runtime verification for multicore embedded controllers that preserves deadline guarantees and sound verdicts despite asynchronous, lossy telemetry.
requirements: Verdicts are sound under telemetry loss and complete for bounded-response violations when telemetry is lossless.
Monitoring adds ≤5% worst-case execution time per control job while preserving all specified deadlines.

nodes.content: Use sequence-numbered per-core rings and completeness-watermarked, skew-aware three-valued monitors; budget instrumentation below 5% and verify deadlines by response-time analysis.
How can completeness watermarks advance past dropped sequence numbers without turning unknown bounded-response outcomes into false violations?
Under ≤200-µs clock skew, gap-tainted windows stay unknown; lossless watermarks detect every bounded-response violation after expiry.
Replay 10,000 gap-injected and lossless traces at ±200-µs skew; check gap taint and violation completeness against an oracle.
Across 10,000 traces at ±200-µs skew, gap-tainted windows stayed unknown; lossless replay detected 100% of violations after expiry.
Adopt gap-tainted unknown verdicts and skew-aware watermarks; replay showed no false violations and complete lossless detection at ±200 µs.
Integrate adopted gap-tainted monitors into the dual-core controller; verify ≤5% per-job WCET overhead and all deadlines via response-time analysis.
Instrument dual-core control jobs with per-core rings; bound per-job WCET overhead against 5% and recalculate fixed-priority response times.
DualCore-RTA v1 report records per-job WCET overhead, fixed-priority response bounds, deadline margins, and 5% budget checks.
Independently recompute DualCore-RTA v1 margins with shared-cache contention and interrupt interference; check every job against 5% overhead and deadlines.
Including cache and interrupt interference, independent DualCore-RTA v1 audit found 4.3% maximum per-job WCET overhead and 0.8-ms minimum deadline margin.
Stress-test dual-core hardware for 24 hours at 10% telemetry loss; compare verdicts to oracle and latencies to DualCore-RTA bounds.
In 24-hour hardware stress at 10% loss, seven false violations followed dropped tail responses before sequence gaps became observable.
Retain timing-qualified per-core rings, but reject current watermark verdict logic: seven false violations violate soundness despite 4.3% overhead.
Require contiguous per-core sequences through post-deadline producer seals before declaring violations; missing seals yield unknown, with sealing off control-job paths.
What post-deadline seal guard certifies cross-core response completeness under ±200-µs clock skew without indefinitely delaying lossless verdicts?
With ≤200-µs publication latency, 600-µs guarded per-core seals and contiguous sequences prevent false violations while retaining lossless completeness.
Run 24-hour dual-core trials with 600-µs seals, ±200-µs skew, ≤200-µs publication, and 0%/10% loss; audit oracle verdicts, WCET, deadlines.
600-µs seals yielded zero false violations at 10% loss, 100% lossless violation detection, 4.3% per-job WCET overhead, no deadline misses.
Using validated 600-µs seals, prove lossy soundness and lossless completeness; certify ≤5% per-job WCET overhead and deadlines.
Model-check 600-µs sealed-ring automata under ±200-µs skew and ≤200-µs publication for lossy soundness and lossless violation completeness.
SealedRing-TLA+ v1 contains the 600-µs seal model, telemetry assumptions, and model-checking results for lossy soundness and lossless completeness.
Use DMA-backed per-core trigger/response traces with producer-fenced epoch certificates; issue violations only for sequence-complete epochs, otherwise unknown.
What DMA fencing and epoch-buffer size prevent undetected wraparound while keeping per-job WCET overhead below 5%?
With ≤10-ms epochs, ≤10-ms DMA lag, and ≤20k events/s/core, 512-entry rings with completion-fenced certificates prevent silent wraparound at ≤5% overhead.
Extend SealedRing-TLA+ v1 with DMA fences; stress 512-entry rings at 20k events/s/core, 10-ms epochs/lag; audit wraparound, ≤5% WCET overhead, deadlines.
At 20k events/s/core and 10-ms DMA lag, 512-entry rings showed zero silent overwrites; maximum per-job WCET overhead was 3.8%.
Extend SealedRing-TLA+ v1 for adversarial DMA fence ordering; stress 512-entry rings at 10-ms lag, checking silent overwrites and ≤5% WCET.
SealedRing-TLA+ found a stale DMA completion fence permitting silent overwrite of a live slot in 512-entry rings at 10-ms lag.
Reject current DMA certificates despite 3.8% overhead: stale fences permit silent overwrites; retain validated 600-µs sealed rings.
Generation-tagged DMA completion fences and 1024-entry rings prevent silent overwrites at 20k events/s/core and 10-ms lag with ≤5% job overhead.
Extend SealedRing-TLA+ v1 to model-check generation-tagged DMA fences; stress 1024-entry rings at 20k events/s/core, 10-ms lag, measuring WCET.
Model-checked generation-tagged fences showed zero silent overwrites at 20k events/s/core, 10-ms lag; measured per-job WCET overhead peaked at 4.6%.
Benchmark generation-tagged DMA against retained 600-µs sealed rings; certify lossy soundness, lossless completeness, ≤5% job overhead, and deadlines.
Extend SealedRing-TLA+ v1 for generation-tagged DMA; compare 600-µs seals at 0%/10% loss, auditing verdicts, WCET, and deadlines.
DMA-versus-SealedRing v1 report compares oracle verdicts at 0%/10% loss, per-job WCET overhead, and deadline margins.
Use admission-bounded shared-SRAM obligation slots with fenced cross-core responses; deadline watchdogs emit certificates, while missing telemetry yields unknown.
What slot capacity and cross-core fence ordering prevent premature watchdog violations without pushing control-job overhead above 5%?
For ≤32 concurrent obligations, 64 slots and release/acquire fences enable producer-sealed absence verdicts after a 600-µs guard at ≤5% overhead.
Using DMA-versus-SealedRing v1 baselines, model-check 64-slot release/acquire interleavings; stress ≤32 obligations with 600-µs guards, auditing verdicts, WCET, deadlines.
64-slot fenced stress found zero false verdicts, 100% lossless violation detection, 4.1% maximum per-job WCET overhead, zero deadline misses.
Against DMA-versus-SealedRing v1, model-check 64-slot reuse under delayed cross-core writes and dropped seals; audit false violations and WCET.
At 32 obligations, a stale seal survived 64-slot reuse; a delayed response caused one false violation despite release/acquire fences.
Reject unversioned obligation slots: 4.1% overhead passes, but stale seals caused a false violation; retain sealed rings as fallback.
Generation-tagged 64-slot obligations, release/acquire seals, and acknowledgment-before-reuse prevent stale-seal violations for ≤32 obligations at ≤5% overhead.
Using DMA-versus-SealedRing v1 baselines, model-check tagged 64-slot reuse with delayed responses and dropped seals; measure per-job WCET and deadlines.
Tagged 64-slot reuse showed zero false violations under delayed responses/dropped seals; WCET overhead peaked at 4.7%, with no deadline misses.
Benchmark e10’s tagged slots against DMA-versus-SealedRing v1 under forced reuse at 32 obligations and 0%/10% loss; audit verdicts, WCET, deadlines.
At forced 32-obligation reuse, acknowledgment contention raised one control job’s WCET overhead to 5.6%, breaching the 5% limit.
Reject generation-tagged slots despite zero false violations: forced reuse raised job overhead to 5.6%; retain 600-µs sealed rings.
128 generation-tagged slots with release/acquire seals and asynchronous reclamation avoid acknowledgment contention at ≤32 obligations and ≤5% overhead.
Recheck 64-slot acknowledgment-before-reuse against DMA-versus-SealedRing v1 under bursty 32-obligation arrivals; measure worst-case job overhead and deadlines.
Under bursty arrivals without forced reuse, tagged 64-slot jobs peaked at 4.8% overhead, with zero false violations or deadline misses.
Model-check 128-slot asynchronous reclamation and benchmark forced reuse at 32 obligations against DMA-versus-SealedRing v1; audit verdicts, WCET, deadlines.
At forced 32-obligation reuse, asynchronous reclamation deferred a seal past its guard, producing two false violations despite 4.2% overhead.
Using DMA-versus-SealedRing v1 baselines, model-check 128-slot reclamation with delayed acknowledgments and 10% loss; audit seal ordering and oracle verdicts.
Without forced reuse, delayed acknowledgments and 10% loss preserved seal ordering in 128-slot reclamation, with zero false violations.
Reject asynchronous reclamation: nonforced trials were sound, but forced reuse caused false violations; retain 600-µs sealed rings.
Finalize 600-µs sealed rings; replay forced-reuse and delayed-acknowledgment traces at 0%/10% loss, certifying soundness, completeness, ≤5% overhead, deadlines.
Replay e13 forced-reuse and e14 delayed-acknowledgment schedules through r3’s 600-µs sealed rings at 0%/10% loss; audit verdicts, WCET, deadlines.
SealedRing-Final v1 contains forced-reuse and delayed-acknowledgment replay traces, oracle verdict comparisons, per-job WCET bounds, and deadline margins.
Independently audit SealedRing-Final v1 for lossless violation completeness, lossy verdict soundness, ≤5% per-job WCET overhead, and deadline margins.
Independent SealedRing-Final v1 audit found zero false verdicts at 10% loss, 100% lossless violation detection, 4.3% overhead, 0.8-ms minimum margin.
Adopt sealed rings: sound, 100% lossless detection, 4.3% overhead, 0.8-ms margin; asynchronous slots fail forced reuse despite sound nonforced runs.
